# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

**1. Start with your revenue reality, not your wishlist**
Pull your last 3 months of booking/payment data. Map what members actually buy most, what coaches deliver most, and what's sitting unused. Build your menu around proven demand first — then add 1-2 premium offerings. Grace: if "small group training" gets booked 3x more than "nutrition coaching," lead with that.

**2. Price by outcome, not by time**
Don't list "1-hour personal training = £50." Instead: "6-Week Strength Foundation (6×1hr sessions) = £240" or "Monthly Unlimited Small Group Access = £89." Members buy outcomes; coaches need to upsell packages, not hourly rates. This also protects your coaches from undercharging for value.

**3. Create two separate, visually different menus**
Internal coach menu (what they can offer, upsell triggers, commission structure) ≠ member-facing menu (clean pricing, results language, no internal margins). Coach version has profit margins and bundling rules. Member version is marketing copy — "Build confidence and strength with your dedicated coach" beats "Personal training available."

**4. Print the member menu in 3 places today**
Reception, studio wall, and email it to your existing member base. Get feedback in week one: which services get questions? That's your clarification opportunity before finalizing. Coaches should also have a laminated pocket version to reference during conversations.

**5. Lock in one rule: no verbal pricing**
Every quote comes from the menu. Stops coaches from undercutting and members from shopping around. Make it easy — QR code on the printed

**Insights**

1. **July was an anomaly, not a breakthrough.** You hit 215 leads at £2/lead in July—that's unsustainably cheap and suggests either a creative that went viral, a targeting loophole, or audience saturation you've now hit. August corrected hard: 82 leads at £5/lead. This isn't failure; it's normalisation. Your true cost/lead sits around £5, not £2.

2. **Close rate stayed solid (29% in Aug vs 13.5% in Jul), but lead quality shifted.** July's 29 sales from 215 leads = 13.5% close rate. August's 24 sales from 82 leads = 29% close rate. You're now attracting fewer but significantly warmer prospects—the cheap July leads were likely low-intent tire-kickers. August's tighter funnel is better.

3. **Unit economics are fragile.** At £5 cost/lead and 29% close rate, you're converting ~1 in 3.4 leads to sale. Your profit per sale (£52) means you need to hold cost/lead below £6–£7 to stay profitable. You're at the edge. One uptick in cost/lead to £6–7 and margin collapses.

---

**Actions**

1. **Pause broad/lookalike audiences; double down on core custom audiences.** Your April–June decline (£6 to £21/lead) suggests audience drift and fatigue. July's cheap leads came from somewhere, but you've burned through that pool. Rebuild: Layer a custom audience of past trial users + website visitors (last 180 days) + email subscribers. Test a 1% LLA of converters only (not all leads). Allocate 60% of budget here.

2. **Test "commitment" creative hooks against "curiosity" hooks.** Your 29% close rate suggests messaging is pre-qualifying well. Test two new angles: (a) outcome-focused ("6 weeks to confidence" / results-led visuals of real members), (b) community/belonging ("Women-only space where you belong"). Run both at 20% budget split against your control.

# THE FORGE — FRACTIONAL CFO BRIEF

## REVENUE — CRITICAL ISSUES

• **Rev/member has collapsed to £99 in August (down from £144 in July, down from £131 average Jan–Mar).** You're adding members (164 vs 137 in July) but revenue per head is falling sharply. Root cause: either heavy discounting on new joiners, or existing members not paying full rate. Audit your membership tiers and new-member pricing immediately — you should be hitting £130+ per member. If new members are below £100, you're onboarding at unsustainable LTV.

• **Churn spiked to 12.8% in May** (vs 3–6% norm). That's 17 members lost in one month on a base of 133 — likely the studio relocation disruption. You've recovered (5.5% Aug), but monitor churn weekly now; any spike above 6% needs root-cause action (staff gaps? class cancellations? messaging failure?).

• **Last 3 months (Jun–Aug) averaged £17,363/month revenue vs prior 3 (Jan–Mar) at £14,508** — solid 19.7% growth in absolute terms. But you're *not* translating member growth into revenue growth at the same rate. July was your best month (£19,764). You need to understand what drove July and replicate it: was it a promotion? Full classes? Upsells (PT, merchandise, class packs)?

• **No visible ancillary revenue** (PT sessions, retail, class packs, nutrition plans). At 137–164 members, you have a captive base. Introduce a £15–25/month add-on tier or one-off PT bookings; even 20% uptake at £20/member = +£550/month gross.

---

## EXPENSES — HIGH SPEND vs REVENUE

• **Cash outflows are erratic and often exceed revenue:** Aug cash out was £28,693 on £16,160 revenue (176% ratio). Jun was £20,644 on £15,765 (131%). Exclude April relocation, but you're running a structural cash burn 15–30% of months. Break down that £28,693 in August: wages, rent, supplies, utilities? If any single line is >40% of revenue, flag it. **Most likely culprit: payroll.** At 164 members and £16k/month revenue, you cannot afford more than £8–10k/month in fixed wages (staff + your salary). What are actual wages + on-costs in Aug?
